dimensions.assessment: Directly affects federal agencies, exclusive labor organizations representing federal employees, and individual labor representatives.
dimensions.evidence: the head of each agency shall charge each labor organization recognized as an exclusive representative of employees of such agency a fee

dimensions.assessment: Imposes significant financial fees on labor organizations and potential adverse employment actions for union representatives who fail to track union time.
dimensions.evidence: a labor representative who uses union time and fails to record such use in the applicable time and attendance tracking system shall be considered absent without leave

dimensions.assessment: Requires labor organizations to pay quarterly fees to agencies, which must then be transferred to the general fund of the Treasury.
dimensions.evidence: The head of an agency shall transfer each payment of a fee charged under paragraph (1) that such head receives to the general fund of the Treasury.

dimensions.assessment: Amends chapter 71 of title 5, United States Code, to add new charging, tracking, enforcement, and penalty requirements.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent statutory requirement for ongoing quarterly fees and compliance evaluations every two years.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes a fee structure for federal employee labor organizations using agency resources and employee time, creating enforcement mechanisms and penalties that could eventually lead to decertification.
